questions.question: 用意面和棉花糖搭的塔里，几个正方形框架一推就歪。最有效的加固办法是什么？
options: 把正方形的四条边都换成两根意面并排，把每条边加粗加固
把正方形放大一圈，让结构更舒展
在每个关节处多塞一颗棉花糖，让连接更牢
在每个正方形里加一根斜意面，把它变成两个三角形
questions.explanation: 三角形三条边一旦定死，怎么推都不变形；正方形即使边很粗、关节很牢，也会被压成菱形。加一根斜杠变成两个三角，就是工程师说的三角加固。
questions.question_en: In a spaghetti-and-marshmallow tower, several square frames sway as soon as they're pushed. What is the most effective fix?
options_en: Double up every side of each square with two strands side by side, thickening and reinforcing it
Make each square bigger so the structure is more spread out
Push an extra marshmallow into every joint to make the connections stronger
Add a diagonal strand of spaghetti across each square, turning it into two triangles
questions.explanation_en: Once a triangle's three sides are fixed, it can't deform however you push it, while a square, even with thick sides and firm joints, still folds into a rhombus. Adding a diagonal to make two triangles is what engineers call triangulation.

questions.question: 同一张纸平铺架在两摞书之间，放一枚硬币就塌；折成瓦楞状后能撑住十几枚。主要原因是什么？
options: 折叠后纸的总重量变大，桥身更压得住
折痕让纸的表面变得更粗糙，硬币不容易滑动，也就不容易把桥压塌
折出的棱和弧像一根根小梁，把压力分散开、撑住了形状
折叠后纸变短，两端搭在书上的部分更多了
questions.explanation: 平纸太薄一压就弯，折成瓦楞或卷成筒后，那些棱和弧成了小梁，分散压力并保持形状，这也是纸箱用瓦楞纸、钢梁做成工字形的道理。纸还是同一张，重量并没有变。
questions.question_en: A flat sheet of paper spanning two stacks of books collapses under one coin; folded into corrugations, the same sheet holds a dozen or more. What's the main reason?
options_en: Folding makes the paper heavier overall, so the bridge sits more firmly
The creases roughen the surface so coins don't slide around, making the bridge less likely to collapse
The folded ridges and curves act like little beams, spreading the load and holding the shape
Folding shortens the paper, so more of each end rests on the books
questions.explanation_en: Flat paper is too thin and bends under any load; corrugated or rolled, its ridges and curves become small beams that spread the force and hold the form, which is why boxes use corrugated card and steel beams are I-shaped. It is the same sheet, so its weight hasn't changed.

questions.question: 搭积木塔时，为什么底座宽、越往上越小、重块放下面的塔更能搭高不倒？
options: 这样每块积木之间的摩擦力更大，彼此卡得更紧
这样塔的形状会更接近三角形，而三角形的三条边互相锁死、不会变形
这样塔的总重量更轻，对底座的压力更小
这样整座塔的重心更低，也更容易落在底座范围之内，不容易翻倒
questions.explanation: 塔倒不倒，看重心有没有落在底座范围内：底宽、下重上轻，重心低又稳，所以高楼大厦多是下大上小。三角形不变形说的是杆件框架的道理，用在积木堆叠上是把两条规矩混在了一起。
questions.question_en: When stacking blocks, why can a tower with a wide base, narrowing upward, with the heavy blocks at the bottom, go higher without falling?
options_en: It increases friction between the blocks so they lock together more tightly
It makes the tower closer to a triangle, whose three sides lock each other and can't deform
It makes the tower lighter overall, putting less pressure on the base
It keeps the tower's center of gravity low and more easily within the footprint of the base, so it's harder to tip over
questions.explanation_en: Whether a tower falls depends on whether its center of gravity stays over the base: a wide, bottom-heavy tower keeps it low and stable, which is why tall buildings are wider at the bottom. Triangles resisting deformation is a principle about frames of struts; applying it to stacked blocks mixes up two different rules.
